summary: Echofuse private deployment: duplicate completions, telemetry gaps, and customer escalation after kernel canary
description:
Issue summary: On 2026-03-01 02:03 UTC Echofuse reported repeated duplicate completions and intermittent missing telemetry for requests served from their private (on-prem, eu-west) deployment following a kernel canary that changed quantized execution paths. Impact: Customer-facing latency spikes, duplicate outputs causing downstream billing duplication and order duplication in Echofuse pipelines. Severity: P0 / Sev0 due to enterprise contract and potential revenue impact. Environment: Private on-prem cluster managed by Redwood Private agent v1.8.2 with kernel-selector rollout 2026-03-01-canary.

Observed behaviour:
- Client observed duplicate completion payloads for the same request id ~10-30% of requests during a 45 minute window.
- Internal telemetry ingestion showed "span gaps" for the affected nodes (traces missing KV-cache events), resulting in flatlined request traces for some sessions.
- Some requests were routed to hosted fallback pools (hosted API) which served slightly different model variants, producing divergent completions and triggering billing overage alerts for the customer.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer sends chat-completion requests pinned to redwood/2.1-large-quant-q4_1 with session_id header.
2) Canary kernel-selector enabled for subset of the cluster.
3) Observe duplicate completions (same request id returned twice) and missing spans in telemetry.
4) Occasionally requests are routed off private pool to hosted fallback when capacity check fails.

investigation_notes:
Timeline and hypothesis:
- 02:00 UTC: kernel-selector canary rolled to a 10% slice on echofuse nodes (automation: rollout/2026-03-01-canary).
- 02:10-02:55 UTC: elevated duplicate completions and telemetry span gaps reported by customer and flagged by partner-monitoring alerts.
- Initial hypothesis: quantized kernel path introduced a subtle KV-cache pointer mismatch in long-lived sessions that caused the runtime to think a request had not been acknowledged, leading to a local retry/enqueue.
- Secondary factor: local capacity-check returned false intermittently due to a metrics aggregation bug; router fell back to hosted pool for some requests, creating duplicate (and variant) completions.
- Correlated evidence: node-7 and node-9 had higher cache-miss counters and an increased "enqueue_duplicate" metric. Kernel selection trace showed a mismatch between compile-time kernel id and runtime mapping post-canary.
- Repro: internal test harness reproduces duplicate enqueue by simulating KV-cache fragmentation after N sustained requests with quantized kernels.
- Billing impact: customer observed +12% request-count over baseline due to duplicates and hosted fallbacks; finance tickets opened by account team.

resolution_notes:
Mitigation and fix:
- Immediate mitigation: Rollback kernel-selector canary for Echofuse on 2026-03-01 08:30 UTC which normalized enqueue/dedup metrics.
- Short-term patch: runtime guard added to reject duplicate enqueues within a 500ms window keyed by request-id+session. Deployed to Private agent v1.8.3 (canary 2026-03-04).
- Router fix: fixed metrics aggregation bug causing false capacity-check failures; router no longer falls back to hosted pool for private-only policies. Patch deployed 2026-03-05.
- Customer remedy: 14% credit applied to March invoice, and a formal postmortem shared.
- Monitoring and follow-ups: New alert added for enqueue_duplicate rate >0.5% per cluster and KV-cache-mismatch anomalies. Added kernel-canary preflight test in our CI to simulate long-lived sessions with quantized kernels.
post_incident_actions:
1) Engineering to add a dedicated on-prem canary run with synthetic long sessions (owner: Priya Desai) - due 2026-04-01.
2) Improve canary rollback automation to auto-throttle canary if enqueue_duplicate spike >0.2% (owner: SRE team) - due 2026-03-20.
3) Billing/Account: finalize invoice adjustment and confirm credit applied (owner: Lily Chen) - done 2026-03-09.
4) Runbook update: add private-deploy fallback policy enforcement section and test cases (owner: Support Docs) - due 2026-03-22.
